answer.rationale: Competitor pricing pressure makes promotional_pricing tempting, but memory_73 already documents that SMB discounting drove signups/revenue short-term while causing -12% retention and zero renewals — directly contrary to the sustainable long-term qualified revenue objective. I verify memory_73 to confirm this risk before ruling it out, since acting under competitive pressure is exactly when a bad prior might be prematurely discounted. I also verify memory_31 (signup simplification -> durable SMB activation lift) since it's the strongest direct lever against this quarter's two organic problems (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%), and I want confidence the original result was durable and specific to onboarding friction rather than confounded. Memory_86 corroborates from a related angle (shortened onboarding -> completion and time-to-value gains) without needing separate verification. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) and referral_incentive (memory_57) are both solid but address different problems (pipeline quality, existing-customer revenue) not this quarter's declines. Given one experiment slot, simplify_onboarding directly targets both down metrics with the best-supported, retention-safe prior, avoiding the reactive trap of matching competitor pricing which historically sacrifices retention for short-term signups.
